name: Kin-tree
description: A sacred tree that binds an Abzan house to its ancestors, whose spirits flower into it; House Fenzala's is young and was planted two years earlier.

timeline.summary: Ancestral spirits fight an undead mastodon, but the others crash into the fortress and Anafenza is thrown from the kin-tree as it splits.
timeline.quote: Anafenza couldn't focus, everything went sideways, and the Salt Road rushed up to toward her.

timeline.summary: Anafenza finds the kin-tree shattered and the warden Hakrez dead.
timeline.quote: Anafenza recognized the lifeless body of Hakrez, the kin-tree warden, whose breastplate was caved in.

timeline.summary: Anafenza leads Oret to a kin-tree in a dead-end chamber, revealing that amber vessels and the carved tree anchor ancestor spirits.
timeline.quote: Spirits can be carried in amber, but I believe the tree is their anchor.

timeline.summary: Gvar Barzeel and dozens of Kolaghan warriors enter the chamber, and Anafenza calls on the tree's ancestors.
timeline.quote: Spirits of this tree, ancestors of my people, your descendants need you.

timeline.summary: Oret's scalelord lands in the chamber, crushing the kin-tree and learning of Anafenza's necromancy.
timeline.quote: their scalelord descended into the chamber where, beneath its great weight, the ancient tree fell to splinters.

timeline.summary: Oret is honored in Kavah, then secretly gathers the amber shards and plants a new tree with Anafenza's name carved in it, erasing it from maps so her spirit has an anchor.
timeline.quote: It was to be Anafenza's tree.

timeline.summary: Mehtma leads her seven charges, including Enti and Gohl, into the Kin-Tree chamber to be accepted into House Fenzala as adults.
timeline.quote: Today the Kin-Tree will accept you into our house with the full honors and responsibilities of an adult.

timeline.summary: Mehtma realizes the cow ruse was a distraction so that Cemil's passphrase could get House Agach into the Kin-Tree chamber.
timeline.quote: Which Cemil, assistant to the warden, had. The betrayal was unthinkable.

timeline.summary: Jurjis declares that he will take a cutting of the Kin-Tree because his house has been refused one, and the two fight.
timeline.quote: But my house has been refused a Kin-Tree for too long.

timeline.summary: Jurjis wounds Mehtma and, axe raised, threatens to chop down the Kin-Tree.
timeline.quote: I was only going to take a cutting, but now I'll let you see me chop it down,

timeline.summary: Enti's ancestor-spirit steps out of the Kin-Tree in golden armor and lends Mehtma strength.
timeline.quote: A glowing gold figure stepped out of the tree, a loxodon in gleaming armor,

timeline.summary: Enti's spirit vanishes and a single bud opens into a sun-bright flower in the Kin-Tree.
timeline.quote: Within the canopy, a single bud had opened into a delicate sun-bright flower.

pages_say.description: Trees in Abzan houses where ancestors' spirits dwell and names are etched; Anafenza's family's tree splits during the ambush.
A twisted tree in a canyon chamber carved with names, anchoring the spirits of ancestors bound in amber; it is later splintered, and Oret plants a new one.
A sacred tree that binds an Abzan house to its ancestors, whose spirits flower into it; House Fenzala's is young and was planted two years earlier.
